Where vouchers are waiting

Each desk in the approval chain, with the value it is holding right now.
Or press View on any card above. The list and its export follow whatever project, vendor and trade filters are set at the top.

In-progress bills — unpaid, by project

Every bill not yet paid, grouped by project, with PR, PO, Audit and Finance sign-off dates and the amount requested.

Vendor contract position — last bill only

One row per vendor contract. Contract value, work done, retention and back charge are read off that vendor’s latest bill; paid is the cash released across all their bills. Click a row to filter the whole dashboard to that vendor.

Bill history —

Every bill raised against this contract, oldest first. The row marked LAST is the one feeding the cards above.

Payments released by month

Cash actually leaving the account.

Contract value by trade

Contract value by trade, from last bills.

Bill register — every bill, all details

Newest first. Every bill of every vendor with the resolved vendor name, bill number, all amounts and every approval date. LAST marks the bill used for that vendor’s cumulative figures.

BOQ & Rate Analysis Management System

Quantity Surveying  |  Estimation  |  Cost Control  |  BOQ Management  ·  Prepared for Sajjad Ahmad

🔧 Local data

Rate band by work category

Lowest, average and highest built-up rate per unit in each category.

Rate completeness

Items whose build-up still has an unrated component. These cannot be priced yet.

Quick actions

BOQ item master & rate library

 
Verified / dated source Dated market indication — no PO backing No dated source — assumption, must be confirmed Formula-driven
Actual purchase rates, as received. Every item received on site, with the rate of its latest GRN and every earlier receipt. Units are in house units: GRNs billed per cubic metre, metre or square metre are converted to Cft, Rft and Sft, and the GRN unit is kept in the history. + Rate DB copies an item’s latest GRN rate into the Rate Database as a verified line, with the GRN, date and vendor written into its remarks.

GRN price register

 

Punjab MRS rate register

 
One rate, everywhere. Every rate analysis references these lines by code, so changing a rate here re-prices every affected item, BOQ line and cost summary instantly. Enter the source and the date you took the rate — the colour follows the source, not the number.

Material, labour & plant rate database

 
V — verified, dated source (PO / GRN / signed quote) I — dated market indication, no PO backing A — assumption or unrated, confirm before use

Project particulars

Printed on the BOQ and cost summary headers.

Bill of Quantities

 

Cost summary

Category split with cost per Sft against covered area.

Bill totals

Note on additions. Overheads and profit are already carried inside each built-up rate (rows G and H of every analysis). The percentages below are a bill-level addition — leave them at zero unless your rates were entered net of overhead and profit, otherwise you will double-count.

Calculation settings

Defaults applied to new analyses and to every generated mix.
House standard build-up. A Material → B Wastage (on material only) → C Labour → D Plant → E Access / cradle → F Transport → subtotal → G Overheads → H Profit → rate per unit. Dry-volume factor 1.54 for concrete, 1.30 for mortar; 50 kg cement bag = 1.250 cft.

Data safety

Everything lives in this browser only. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.
Back up regularly. Clearing browser data, switching device or using a private window will lose the rate library. Export the JSON backup after any significant editing session.
Hard reset. Wipes every item, rate, BOQ line and setting stored in this browser and rebuilds the library from the seeded defaults. This cannot be undone.

Import items from CSV

Column headers are matched automatically. Rows with problems are listed rather than silently dropped.
Expected columns (any order, case-insensitive): Category, Sub-category, Description, Specification, Unit, Material Rate, Labour Rate, Plant Rate, Wastage %, Overhead %, Profit %. Any missing numeric column is read as zero and the item is flagged unrated.
